body: The fallback chain now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which differs per site in multisite and can change at runtime. But the translation LRU cache in `translate_accelerator.rb` is keyed only on `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. Once a fallback value is cached for one site (e.g. site A with default `fr`), another site in the same process with the same user locale but default `de` gets site A's text. The stale value also survives a change to default_locale. The cache key needs to include the fallback chain (or at least the site default locale).

Fallback locales are only loaded here, inside the controller `set_locale` filter. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks and any other non-request code call `I18n.t` directly. `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`, so the fallback locales (site default, `:en`) never get loaded there. Missing keys then come back as 'translation missing' instead of falling back. Loading the fallbacks belongs inside `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` (e.g. load every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]`) rather than in one controller hook.

`translate` only ensures `config.locale` is loaded. Calls that pass an explicit `locale:` option (common in mailers/jobs, e.g. `I18n.t(key, locale: user.effective_locale)`) skip loading that locale and its fallbacks. With `Backend::Fallbacks` iterating over `I18n.fallbacks[options[:locale]]`, those locales may not be loaded, so the lookup silently fails. `ensure_loaded!` should run for the requested locale's full fallback chain inside `translate`.

`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` is evaluated on every fallback lookup, i.e. on every missed translation for each locale in the chain. Lookups with args bypass the cache entirely. That puts a SiteSetting read on a very hot path. It also runs during boot, before site settings are available (e.g. an initializer calling I18n.t with a missing key), which can raise.

Fallbacks used to be enabled only in production/profile (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true`). This initializer now enables them in every environment, including test and development. Missing translations in the default locale will now silently show English instead of surfacing as 'translation missing', which hides missing-key bugs in specs. Consider gating this or keeping the missing-translation checks in test.

Subclassing `Hash` while overriding only `[]` gives a half-working object. `fetch`, `key?`, `each`, `inspect` etc. all behave as an empty hash, which is inconsistent with `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, the type other code and gems expect from `I18n.fallbacks` (e.g. calls to `I18n.fallbacks.defaults=`, `map`, or `fetch`). Subclass `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, or at least avoid inheriting Hash semantics that don't apply.
